_note: Every sentence the Flight Director can say. {placeholders} are filled in by src/ai/flightDirector.ts, which decides WHICH line to use; the words themselves all live here.

why.insertionFuel: You reached {target} but could not slow down into orbit: the tank ran dry at the braking burn.
why.powerLow: At {target} your {power} {make} {powerMade} W, but the instruments need {powerNeeded} W, so not everything could run.
why.weakAntenna: Only {dataPct}% of the science data reached Earth, because the {antenna} is too weak for this distance.
why.weakAntennaNoBigger: Only {dataPct}% of the science data reached Earth: your instruments make more data than even the {antenna} can send from {target}.
why.stormNoBackup: A solar storm burned out the electronics: the spacecraft kept working through it with no backup systems.
why.dustIgnored: Dust settled on the solar panels and you let it stay, so the spacecraft flew on with less power.
why.driftIgnored: You ignored the course drift and got lucky: the spacecraft still found {target}.
why.driftIgnoredLost: You ignored the course drift and the spacecraft missed {target}.
why.overCarriedFuel: You reached {target} with far more fuel than needed: the tank could give {dvAvailable} km/s and the trip needed {dvNeeded} km/s.
why.overSizedPanels: You reached {target}, but your {power} make {panelOutput} W when {powerNeeded} W would do.
why.perfect: A perfect flight: you reached {target}, went into orbit and brought home all the science.
why.perfectSomeDataLost: A perfect flight: you reached {target}, went into orbit and sent home everything the antenna could manage from that far away ({dataPct}% of the data).
why.overBudget: This design costs ${costM}M but the budget is ${budgetM}M, so it never left the launch pad.
why.lost: The spacecraft was lost on the way to {target}: {reason}
why.good: You reached {target} and collected {science} of {scienceMax} science points.
why.goodOverPlan: You reached {target} and collected {science} science points — {extra} more than the {scienceMax} you planned for.

tips.insertionFuel: Carry a fuel reserve: a correction burn or a dust shake can eat a small margin.
tips.powerLow: Far from the Sun, choose bigger panels or a nuclear battery, and shake dust off when you can.
tips.weakAntenna: The large dish antenna sends ten times more data home.
tips.weakAntennaNoBigger: Fewer instruments, or ones that make less data, get more of the science home from that far away.
tips.stormNoBackup: In a storm, switch the instruments off, or fly a large bus with backup systems.
tips.dustIgnored: Shaking the panels costs a little fuel but keeps every instrument running.
tips.driftIgnored: A small correction burn early is far cheaper than missing the planet.
tips.overCarriedFuel: Less fuel means less mass, a smaller rocket and money saved for science.
tips.overSizedPanels: Small panels would have done the job here and saved mass and money.
tips.perfect: Try a harder mission, or the fast route with the same design.
tips.overBudget: A lighter rocket, fewer instruments or less fuel brings the cost down.
tips.lost: Check the decisions below to see where it went wrong.
tips.good: Look at the decisions below to see where the missing points went.
tips.goodFullScience: You brought home every science point there was. Try a harder mission, or the fast route with the same design.

decisions.chanceThatCaused: Taking the chance on day {causeDay} paid off and brought {event} on day {eventDay}.
decisions.cause: {event} on day {eventDay} came from your choice on day {causeDay}: {option}.
decisions.chance: You took the chance on day {day} and it paid off: {option}.
decisions.everySafe: Every choice was the safe one. The science you lost on day {day} ({option}) was the price of safety.
decisions.everyGood: Every choice you made on the way was a good one. On day {day} you chose: {option}.
decisions.best: Your best choice was on day {day}: {option}.
decisions.riskiest: Your riskiest choice was on day {day}: {option}.

compare.sameRocket: Like {mission}, you also flew on a {rocket} rocket.
